clock_model.rtl_boundary: phase_clk_i advances phi1-high, non-overlap, phi2-high, and non-overlap digital subphases; the normalized CPU advances after the final subphase
clock_model.historical_boundary: MC6800 receives two non-overlapping phi1 and phi2 clock inputs and transfers bus data during phi2; phi1_o and phi2_o are FPGA integration projections rather than historical output pins
clock_model.limitation: Digital phase ordering and trailing-phi1 processor-control sampling are implemented; nanosecond pulse widths, separation, setup/hold, clock pads, and dynamic-storage limits are not

signals.name: phase_clk_i
signals.fact: four enabled rising edges represent one complete MC6800 bus cycle without using either projected phase as an internal clock

signals.name: phase_reset_n_i
signals.fact: asynchronously initializes the subphase and sampled-control state; distinct from historical RESET

signals.name: clock_enable_i
signals.fact: low holds subphase and normalized CPU state

signals.name: reset_n_i
signals.fact: asynchronous active-low device reset passed to the normalized MC6800 wrapper

signals.name: irq_n_i
signals.fact: sampled at the trailing phi1 boundary and held through the normalized cycle

signals.name: nmi_n_i
signals.fact: sampled at the trailing phi1 boundary; the underlying wrapper retains observed falling edges

signals.name: halt_n_i
signals.fact: sampled at the trailing phi1 boundary before instruction-completion handling

signals.name: tsc_i
signals.fact: high releases address/RW ownership and holds subphase advancement; documented use asserts it while phi1 is high and phi2 low

signals.name: dbe_i
signals.fact: direct data-output qualifier; tie to phi2_o for the manufacturer's normal bus connection or gate independently for documented DMA timing

signals.name: data_i
signals.fact: read byte remains available through projected phi2 and is consumed at the normalized cycle boundary

signals.name: phi1_o
signals.fact: high only in subphase zero and never overlaps phi2_o

signals.name: phi2_o
signals.fact: high only in subphase two and never overlaps phi1_o

signals.name: bus_phase_o
signals.fact: zero phi1, one separation, two phi2, and three separation

signals.name: address_o
signals.fact: normalized cycle address stable throughout the four projected subphases

signals.name: address_oe_o
signals.fact: disabled by BA or TSC through the underlying device wrapper

signals.name: data_o
signals.fact: normalized write byte

signals.name: data_oe_o
signals.fact: enabled only when DBE, VMA, and write direction are simultaneously active

signals.name: read_not_write_o
signals.fact: one for read and zero for write

signals.name: read_not_write_oe_o
signals.fact: disabled by BA or TSC

signals.name: vma_o
signals.fact: qualifies documented valid memory cycles and is forced low during reset, BA, or TSC

signals.name: ba_o
signals.fact: reports HALT or WAI bus release and is forced low by reset or TSC

halt_interrupt_behavior: HALT, IRQ, and NMI are sampled at trailing phi1; HALT completes the current instruction, while requests seen during HALT remain pending until release and acknowledgement in the normalized wrapper
